title: Props, every state
prompt: Paint one sheet of cut-out puppet parts for a paper-puppet film, using the attached image. Panel A is the exact layout, panel B is our footage for these props (reference: copy the object, not the photo style), panel C is the style. STYLE (panel C): flat cards cut from corrugated cardboard, gouache with confident ink linework, the flutes faintly showing through the paint, a thin raw kraft-brown cut edge round every card, brass split-pin brads; shot flat-on, even light, no shadows, no perspective. Copy the craft from C, not the clothes in it. WHAT (panel B): the props of the poem 'How to Win My Heart', one row each, every state of a prop in its own cell, left to right: the small café table and chair: small round metal bistro table and a metal bistro chair, dark green paint worn to grey, on wet stone (empty, with espresso cup, gripped at the edge, chair empty at the end); the five love stories: five folded handwritten letters in a heap on the quay stones; edges catch, curl and blacken one at a time (heap, whole, first catching, three gone, last page in his hand, embers); the harvest: scarlet poppies and purple blossoms: long-stemmed scarlet poppies with black centres and purple blossom spikes, cut and gathered in the crook of his arm; the same flowers then grow out of his hands, shoulders and crown (single stem gripped, armful growing, armful full, emptying into him, blooming from the body); the distant window: a gabled far wall of bonded brick across the water with one lit window, a mullion, a sill, and a woman in red in it (out of focus, wall resolving, her shape resolving, eyes met, lit, held); Jupiter and its moons: a big banded planet low over the harbor in cream and rust, four small cratered moons coming out one by one (planet only, day-pale, first moon, three, four, counted); the two moored boats: small wooden boats with a mast, lying over on the mud at low tide, upright and afloat by the end (aground, lying over, lifting, afloat, sailing out (one)); espresso cup: white espresso cup on a saucer (held, on the table); the sunglasses: the poet's black sunglasses (on, pinched off, held low); pearls and rosary: a long strand of white pearls; a wooden rosary loop (clutched); the quay rail: black iron rail along the quay edge (plain). Paint each state as a flat cardboard prop card at the size its cell gives, the same object across its row; a brass brad on the green cross (its pivot); where there is a red cross, that is where a hand grips it. LAYOUT (panel A): paint one card inside each grey ghost, in the same place, size and angle, inside its dashed outline; a brass brad exactly on every green cross; each red cross must fall inside that card's rounded end. NEVER draw a pelvis, hip, shorts or briefs card (the thighs end in a rounded seat that tucks under the hem), a sleeveless vest, lace-up boots, or sunglasses painted onto a head. OUTPUT: only the painted cards on a pure white 2048x1152 sheet laid out as panel A. Leave out panels B and C, the crosses, labels, ruler, dashed lines and ghosts.
